This report develops, tests, and critically evaluates a wavelet-based trading framework for\
commodity futures. Starting from the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) as introduced by\
Torrence and Compo \[1\], we build a fully causal, walk-forward pipeline for extracting band\
limited cyclical components from commodity log-returns, gate their use by formal statistical\
significance against a red-noise null, and combine them with a Hidden Markov Model (HMM)\
regime classifier and cross-wavelet analysis against macroeconomic drivers. Every stage is sub\
jected to an out-of-sample discipline: bootstrap confidence intervals, train/test band selection,\
and rolling multi-window validation. The central empirical finding is not that the wavelet sig\
nal generates a stable, exploitable alpha on its own-- it does not, once look-ahead bias and\
multiple-testing effects are controlled for-- but that wavelet-detected cyclical power is strongly\
and independently confirmed (via HMM) to concentrate in high-volatility market regimes, and\
that this same information, used as an inverse risk-reduction overlay rather than a directional\
bet, materially improves the risk-adjusted profile of a diversified mean-reversion ensemble while\
failing on a directional buy-and-hold exposure-- a distinction with a clear economic explana\
tion. The report is organized to first establish the theory, then the methodology, then the\
validation framework, and finally the empirical results and their interpretation
